chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abdul Hameed Al-Taiy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'Can I marry the woman and consummate the marriage with her without giving her anything?' He said, 'Yes, it becomes a debt upon you for her.'

key_terms.أَدْخُلُ بِهَا: Consummate the marriage (enter into the wife)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry and consummate the marriage before paying the dowry?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the payment of the dowry (mahr) is not a prerequisite for the validity of the marriage contract or consummation, but rather creates an immediate debt (dayn) upon the husband once the wife is entered into. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that while the wife is entitled to her dowry from the moment of marriage, the husband's failure to pay does not invalidate the union, though it remains a financial obligation enforceable by the wife. This ruling underscores the flexibility in marital contracts while ensuring the wife's financial rights are preserved as a secured debt.
